subject: Privacy questionnaire — PII classification, KMS custody & access diagram request
body_messages:
From: privacy@medicapp.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@medicapp.com
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: MedicApp security questionnaire — PII handling clarifications

Hi Grace,

Thanks for agreeing to help—attached is our privacy questionnaire (first tab is the high-priority sections). Before we complete the vendor assessment, we need quick clarifications so our InfoSec/Legal reviewers can proceed:

1) Can you confirm which PII categories Redwood classifies as "sensitive" versus "standard" in your processing inventory? We need the list by field (e.g., name, email, national id, health conditions).

2) Key custody: does Redwood hold encryption keys for customer data in hosted mode, or are keys customer-managed (KMS/HSM integrations)? If Redwood holds keys in any supported flow, please identify where keys are stored and which subprocessors may have access.

3) Data flow diagram: please provide a diagram showing ingress (customer API call), transit encryption, caching layers (KV cache), and any persistent stores. We need to know which network boundaries cross regions.

4) Subprocessors: do you have any planned additions in the next 60 days that will touch logs or PII? If so, list name, country, and high-level purpose.

We attached our questionnaire (MedicApp_Privacy_Questionnaire_20270403.xlsx). Happy to sync via call if it's easier.

Thanks,
Samuel Cho
Privacy Lead, MedicApp
privacy@medicapp.com

[Attachment: MedicApp_Privacy_Questionnaire_20270403.xlsx]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
To: privacy@medicapp.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 03 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedicApp security questionnaire — PII handling clarifications

Samuel — thank you for the clear list and the spreadsheet. Attaching a short packet to start: the redwood-data-flow-v2.png (diagram) and a KMS custody summary PDF. High-level answers below; we'll fill the questionnaire spreadsheet in the next 48 hours and flag any rows where we need MedicApp input.

1) PII classification: Redwood maintains an internal classification where we treat PHI (health conditions, diagnoses), national identifiers (SSN, national ID), and biometric data as "highly sensitive". Names, emails, phone numbers, and device identifiers are "standard PII" unless combined with health data or identifiers. We'll map the questionnaire fields to our categories in the completed spreadsheet.

2) Key custody: for Redwood Hosted (default) we currently manage keys in our cloud KMS with customer-scoped key material sealed under our HSM-backed service; access to key material is restricted to our crypto service accounts. We offer two alternatives for customers with stricter custody requirements: (a) Bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via customer-managed KMS integration (supports AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault), and (b) Dedicated Private deployments where the keys are exclusively customer-managed and stored in the customer's VPC/HSM. When Redwood-hosted keys are used, we do not hand over raw key material to subprocessors. Subprocessors may have access to encrypted artifacts but not to KMS plaintext. We'll attach a KMS attestation describing access controls.

3) Data flow diagram: attached redwood-data-flow-v2.png shows the ingress -> routing -> runtime -> KV cache -> optional cache-to-disk for cold-starts -> async logs & metrics pipeline. Sensitive fields are redacted in logs by default; customers can opt-in to additional logging. The diagram includes region boundaries and indicates where data is encrypted in transit and at rest.

4) Subprocessors: no planned additions in the next 60 days that will touch PII. Current subprocessors that could see derived telemetry or log artifacts are listed in the DPA annex; we'll extract and include them in the completed questionnaire.

Next steps: we'll: (a) fill in the questionnaire rows you marked high-priority, (b) provide the KMS attestation (attached), and (c) offer a 30-minute walkthrough if you'd like.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Manager, Privacy and Compliance
Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

[Attachments: redwood-data-flow-v2.png; kms-key-custody-attestation-2027-03.pdf]

From: samuel.cho@medicapp.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@medicapp.com
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedicApp security questionnaire — PII handling clarifications

Grace — this is very helpful, thank you. A couple of follow-ups from our InfoSec reviewer: 

- For Hosted KMS: can you confirm whether any Redwood employees have the ability to decrypt customer request payloads for debugging (i.e., privileged log access with key unwrap)? If yes, what controls are in place (JUST-MIN, break-glass, audit)?

- The diagram shows a KV cache in the runtime. Does that cache ever persist session-level PII to disk? If so, what is the retention and who can access those artifacts?

- For subprocessors: our legal wants a simple CSV of the current list with (name, country, role, whether they have access to PII). We need it attached to the completed questionnaire.

Would appreciate short, bullet answers so we can move the assessment through our approval workflow. If it's easier, we can take the 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow.

Best,
Sam
Privacy Lead, MedicApp

[MedicApp: spreadsheet notes in rows 2-8 marked "urgent"]

From: marcus_lin@redwood.ai
To: samuel.cho@medicapp.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MedicApp security questionnaire — PII handling clarifications

Sam — thanks for the clear list. Short answers below (I'll also attach the CSV and a brief proof-of-controls snapshot):

- Employee decrypt ability: Redwood engineers do not have standing decryption capabilities for customer request payloads. Decryption for debugging requires a documented break-glass request reviewed by Security + Product Ops, approved by a senior manager, and executed by the Crypto team. All such events are logged to an immutable audit trail and retained for 7 years. We enforce least-privilege via role-based permissions and ephemeral privileged sessions; requests are time-limited and require justification.

- KV cache persistence: runtime KV cache is memory-first. We do have an optional cold-storage mechanism that persists encrypted cache shards to SSD for cold-start recovery; by default that feature is off for hosted customers unless explicitly enabled. When enabled, persisted shards are encrypted at rest with keys described in the KMS attestation. Retention defaults to 24 hours for cache shards, configurable up to 7 days with customer agreement. Access to persisted shards is restricted to the runtime service account and audited; human access requires the break-glass process above.

- Subprocessor CSV: attached (subprocessors-current-20270405.csv) with the requested columns. No subprocessor we list has access to plaintext KMS keys; most access is to encrypted telemetry or anonymized metrics.

We can do a 30-minute walkthrough tomorrow at 11:00 PT — Grace will send calendar invite if that works.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference

[Attachments: subprocessors-current-20270405.csv; proof-of-controls-snapshot.txt]
